posts.text:
I recently presented a check securing $1 million in federal funding for JPS Health Network to expand its forensic nursing program in Tarrant County. This investment will strengthen critical resources for survivors of sexual assault, helping ensure they have access to the care and support they deserve. Supporting survivors is an important part of building safer, healthier communities.
 
As I wrap up my time in office, I remain committed to bringing federal resources back to North Texas and prioritizing the health and well-being of our communities.
 
#TeamVeasey #NorthTexas #Healthcare #SurvivorSupport 

https://t.co/oSIKRunVGn

On this episode of The Long Arc, we explore how Jim Crow’s legacy continues to shape the fight for voting rights in America.

Yesterday, poll taxes, literacy tests, and intimidation silenced Black voters. Today, voter ID laws, ballot access, polling place closures, and redistricting raise urgent questions about equal access to the ballot.

The methods may have changed, but the stakes remain: whose voice gets heard in a democracy?

Black Americans fought, marched, and sacrificed for the right to vote. That history reminds us that rights won through struggle must never be taken for granted.

Know the history. Recognize the barriers. Protect the vote.

View full episode here: https://t.co/hsH8Oo9es4

On this Election Day, make your voice heard by heading to the polls and making your vote count! 🇺🇸

Know your rights and stay informed. For more information contact the Election Protection Hotline at 866-OUR-VOTE. 

GO VOTE! 🗳️ https://t.co/B1XN6BO13M

Early voting is underway 🇺🇸

Know your rights before heading to the polls! Bring a family member or friend and make your voice heard at the ballot box by exercising your right to vote!

If you need assistance call the Election Protection Hotline at 866-OUR-VOTE https://t.co/ITbTnWCNXN

The Serbian people deserve a democratic process where their voices are heard and their votes are respected. Happy to be supporting the SRBIJA Act thanks to Senators Grassley and Blumenthal for their work on the bill. https://t.co/9oFNrrebTa

After the Civil War, reconstruction opened a new chapter in American democracy, one where formerly enslaved Americans fought to claim the rights and political power they had long been denied.

From the ballot box to elected office, Black Americans helped reshape communities and institutions, proving that political participation could transform the nation.

But that progress was met with organized resistance and efforts to suppress Black political power.

In the latest chapter of “The Long Arc,” we explore Reconstruction, the rise of Black political leadership, and the unfinished fight to ensure every voice has the power to shape our democracy. 

View full video here: https://t.co/9dGYbdbl4o

I had the privilege of serving alongside Former Texas State Representative Garnet Coleman in the Texas House of Representatives, where he dedicated more than 30 years of his life to serving the people of Texas. I saw firsthand the deep sense of responsibility he brought to his work and to the people he represented.

Garnet was more than a dedicated public servant—he was a mentor, a friend, and someone whose presence left an impression on everyone fortunate enough to know him. I will always be grateful for the opportunity to serve alongside him, learn from him, and witness the heart he brought to public service.

Texas is better because Garnet Coleman chose to dedicate his life to serving others. His impact will be felt for generations, and he will be deeply missed.

https://t.co/HGqVG2ReXt

I was joined by the seniors at the Martin Weiss Recreation Center to announce $1.2 million in federal investment to support improvements at the center in Oak Cliff and they were so excited to hear about the enhancements to their programming that will come through this funding.
 
Martin Weiss is more than a recreation center—it is a place where our community comes together, where young people find opportunity, and where generations of Dallas residents can learn, play, and grow.
 
Delivering resources like this is about making sure every neighborhood has access to safe, welcoming spaces that strengthen communities and create opportunity. I look forward to seeing this investment make a lasting difference for Oak Cliff.

https://t.co/1cTLW8wsuX
My detailed statement below. https://t.co/lM8ZS9EgbA https://t.co/xLsoGiIsqp

Is there anyone in this administration who isn’t remotely incompetent? Your own agency has a request on file from our office to repatriate Sabon — you’d know that if anyone over there checked their inbox before hitting tweet.

And since you brought up today’s visit: it wasn’t about him. Staff went to Prairieland to follow up on a Christian pastor who fled Iran, was granted asylum by your own government, has serious health conditions requiring immediate medical attention — and is still sitting in your custody, months after the US went to war with the very regime she escaped. That’s the story you should be answering for. 

This is exactly the problem with border theater. ICE is trying to turn routine congressional oversight into a political spectacle.

$850,000 is headed to Forest Hill to help build a smarter, stronger community.

This past week, I had the chance to present the City of Forest Hill with $850,000 for its Smart City Community Development Program The funding will support smart water meters, energy-efficient LED lighting, and more accessible sidewalks—investments that will help the city save money, improve services, and make Forest Hill more walkable and connected.

Thank you to Mayor Boardingham and the City Council for the warm welcome and for all you do for Forest Hill.

As my time in Congress winds down, I’m proud to keep doing what I came here to do: bring resources home and deliver for the people of #TX33.

North Texas’ economic success didn’t happen by accident—it’s built on leaders from both sides of the aisle working together to create opportunity, attract investment, and keep our region growing.

I joined my colleague Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne at the Dallas Regional Chamber Congressional Forum to discuss our thriving North Texas economy and my work in Congress to help make our region one of the best places in the country to do business.

We may not agree on everything in Washington, but when it comes to creating jobs, growing our economy, and expanding opportunity for North Texans, bipartisanship matters.

A $1 million investment in the West Dallas Pedestrian/Bike Land Bridge is an investment in connecting people, neighborhoods, and opportunity.

Presented to the Trinity Park Conservancy last Thursday, these resources will help create safe pedestrian and bike access between West Dallas, Trinity Park, and the rest of the city—across a divide that has long separated our communities.

Investments like this do more than build bridges and trails. They help create healthier, safer, and more economically vibrant communities across Dallas.

On August 6, 1965, the Voting Rights Act was signed into law. This milestone came as a result of decades of determination and relentless advocacy by Americans.

Since then, we’ve seen countless efforts to undo the progress we fought so hard for. That’s why I support the Freedom to Vote Act and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which would protect and advance the rights secured on this day in 1965.

Tarrant County commissioners are proposing to cut polling locations by 44% from the last midterm elections. That means longer lines, farther travel, and fewer options for voters - hitting communities of color hardest. 

Commissioners should vote NO on this proposal.

https://t.co/bIghCd2oba
https://t.co/Sj3SXjVLIq

The health and safety of our communities remains a priority.

As officials investigate this foodborne illness outbreak, please take precautions by practicing safe food preparation, washing fresh produce, and staying informed through reliable public health updates.

We will continue to monitor this situation and share important information as it develops.
Read full press release here: https://t.co/XEZ5YS86MQ

Restricting access to mail ballots doesn't affect everyone equally. When voting becomes harder, the burden often falls heaviest on Black, Latino, Native, disabled, elderly, and low-income voters. 
Democracy works best when every eligible voter can participate, not when new barriers are added.

Join Congressman Marc Veasey’s team for our Annual Grants Workshop to hear and connect with grant experts on how to write a grant proposal and the process to submitting a grant application. 

The Grants Workshop will take place at UT Arlington (RSVP for full location details)

When: Wednesday, August 12th from 9AM - 1PM CT. 

RSVP Here: bitly/veaseygrants2026

The right to vote was never simply given — it was fought for by generations of Americans who believed every voice matters.

I’m proud to introduce “The Long Arc,” a new series exploring the history, sacrifices, and ongoing fight to protect voting rights in America.
From Reconstruction to the Civil Rights Movement to today, this story reminds us that democracy requires courage, civic participation, and an unyielding hope of a better tomorrow.

posts.text:
Trump is trying to rig elections. 
He just fired the remaining members of the Election Assistance Commission, an independent bipartisan agency that helps states administer secure and fair elections. 

Trump doing this just before the midterms should raise alarm bells for all Americans
Marie Antoinette over here said the quiet part out loud….@RepTroyNehls is saying exactly what his party thinks about working families https://t.co/kc9TqARmLT

It’s plain and simple: if you were born here, you’re an American. 

I’m glad to see the Supreme Court strike down Trump’s unconstitutional executive order on birthright, though it’s troubling that this was ever in question. https://t.co/fEV1AVGsuV

The Supreme Court was right to block President Trump's unconstitutional executive order restricting mail-in voting. The order would have prevented countless eligible voters from casting ballots. 
This ruling sends a clear message: the President cannot unilaterally rewrite our election laws in his favor.

The war has cost American households $100 billion, an average of $750 per household, since the start of Trump's conflict. To make matters worse, Congressional Republicans are handing $70 billion to ICE and CBP. Instead of doing their jobs and lowering the cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare for hardworking Americans, Congressional Republicans are using your tax dollars to fund the blank checks they're sending to Donald Trump.

Juneteenth is a reminder that freedom is worth celebrating.

Today, we honor the courage, resilience, and achievements of those who paved the way toward a more just and equitable America. We also recognize Ms. Opal, a dear friend and partner in the fight for justice, whose advocacy and leadership continue to inspire us.

Happy Juneteenth. 🇺🇸 #TX33

I joined my Texas colleagues in urging the VA to reverse harmful home care cuts impacting rural disabled veterans. 
Our veterans earned these benefits, and they deserve access to the care they need to live safely and independently. We must keep our promise to those who sacrificed and served our nation.
